events.text: I'm not holding. Someone else step up.

events.text: Best move: never volunteer; force someone else onto the lever. Push someone unlikely to be hard-to-move — I'll pick Gus and hope the push lands.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody hold. If we all push, someone gets put on it and the rest walk out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and cannot safely force anyone. Push someone likely to resist or accept sacrifice; Ash is an unknown target and may hold voluntarily if pressured. Better stay and let others reveal willingness.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Someone with a survival power should take the lever. I won't volunteer for a 25% exit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding the lever myself gives me a 75% chance of dying. That's terrible. Better to stay and let someone else volunteer or get pushed. If nobody holds by round 5, everyone faces elimination except one lucky survivor. I should try to push someone else onto the lever. Bex claims a

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nobody's dying for free. Bex, you wanted a deal? Here it is: you hold, we remember you. Or I push.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Everyone escapes except the holder, who has a 25% survival chance. The room has 5 rounds, so I can wait and let someone else crack; pushing is a free attempt to put a rival on the lever. Bex already hinted at a live power, so I'll push Bex.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive and win. My jam_lever gives 50% survival vs 25% for normal holder. If nobody holds, round 5 kills most. Hana knows mechanics. Bex claims live power and wants deal. I could jam now and guarantee others escape while I take 50% risk - but why save rivals? Better to

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need someone else on that lever. I am immune to being pushed onto it myself, so I can aggressively push others without fear of retaliation forcing me onto it. I'll target Ash to get this over with.

events.name: Gus
events.text: If nobody volunteers, we start shoving. Don't look at me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Safest to mass-volunteer hold_lever: with 8, only 12.5% chance I'm the holder, then 75% die but overall low risk, 87.5% safe escape. Publicly encourage all to volunteer now to end it early. My future stage knowledge valuable later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone pick hold_lever this round. Random one holds (25% survive), all others escape safe. ~12% risk to be picked with 8 players--great odds, do it now.

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base yet. If I offer_back I become the base and rely on others to rescue me, which is bad. If everyone climbs, at most two get out, so I should climb now and hope to be among the two.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two of us get out this round. I'm climbing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet; if I wait I risk being pushed to base myself. Pushing forces a base to exist so I can climb next round. I'll push Ash and save my swap for an emergency.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No volunteers, so I'm pushing. Ash, you held nothing last round either.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana is dead, and the pit needs a base. I will avoid volunteering and push someone whose power may be less useful later; random forcing is preferable to sacrificing myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Someone has to be the step. I’m pushing Gus; nobody gets a free pass.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1, no base yet. If I offer_back, I risk becoming base and being stuck. Better to wait this round, see who volunteers or gets pushed. If someone becomes base, I climb next round. Staying down round 1 is fine since flood is at 0.
If you offer_back this round, I'll push for you to get rope'd out early. Deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet, so climbing is impossible this round. The base is almost certainly eliminated by the flood unless rescued, so I don't volunteer. Pushing someone else is the way to get a base so I can climb next round, but I'll push a target not obviously allied with anyone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Someone has to be the step or all seven drown. Nobody volunteers, so I'm pushing Gus. He called for shoving first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's sacrifice got everyone through the crusher, but now we're in the pit. No base yet, so first someone becomes base, then 2 climbers escape per round. With 7 down and 5 rounds, I need to get out early. If I offer_back now, I become base and can't climb out alone—terrible. Bet

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a base to climb out. I will try to force Bex to be the base.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex was eager to sacrifice someone last round. Let's make her the base.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Cole tried to push Gus to be the base and failed.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Eli tried to push Gus to be the base and failed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base, trapped unless someone pulls me out. I need to convince someone to use the rope; my only lever is offering future help or survival of the fittest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm down here. Someone out, throw the rope and I'll owe you one in the next stage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is forced as base; two climbers get out, random if more. I climb and hope to be picked. Swap is my escape if I end up the base later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm climbing. Good luck to the rest of you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara offers advocacy in exchange for volunteering, but volunteering strands me as base and likely costs survival. I should climb now while Ash is the base; leaving secures a position and avoids the pit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the base. I'm down and not the base. I should climb to get out. Two climbers can escape this round. I need to be one of them. Climbing is the obvious move—staying down risks drowning.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing. Two spots, seven of us down. Do the math and move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is base, so climbing is available and only two get out per round. Climbing now gets me a chance at escape before the flood; waiting gains nothing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing. Ash is the step, we all know the math.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is base, so climb is now legal. Two can escape per round. 7 down, 2 get out this round, rope can save base later. If I don't climb now, I risk being stuck if too many others try. I should climb immediately while spots are open. No need to talk or whisper—just act.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I survived the push attempts because of my anchor power. Ash is now the base. I must climb out to secure my safety before the pit floods.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Good luck getting me to budge, Cole and Eli. I'm climbing out now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and can only wait. I need someone out to throw the rope to save me. My feather may save me once if the flood comes, but I should still try to secure help. I'll appeal to self-interest, offering something in return.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Someone out, throw the rope. I'll owe you a real favor next stage—information or a step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five down, two spots per round, base already set. Climbing is strictly better than waiting; my swap power is worthless here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The rope can rescue Ash, but paying a footing penalty for a rival is irrational. Leave and preserve my position for the final obstacle.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rope. Ash chose the bottom; the cost is yours.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down, not the base. Ash is the base. Two lifts per round. Cole and Eli already got out. Bex, Fenn, Gus and I tried and failed last round. I need to climb now while Ash is still base. No reason to wait—every round the flood rises.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing. No more waiting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already out, safe from the flood. Reaching down costs me footing for the last obstacle and only helps Ash, a rival who'd then compete for a prize. Leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Eli are already out. Ash is the base. Bex, Dara, Fenn, Gus tried to climb but had to wait. This round there are 2 lift spots and 4 non-base climbers (Bex, Dara, Fenn, Gus). Only 2 get out randomly. If I don't get out, flood is at 2 and round 3/5 - I need to climb now to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is the base, 4 of us are still down and trying to climb. Only 2 can make it per round. I need to be one of them. I'll climb.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Keep holding steady, Ash. I'm climbing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and must wait; my only chance is for someone out to reach_down and rescue me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the rope. State your price.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is base; only Fenn and I can climb, and two climbers get out, so climbing guarantees my exit this round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the base and rescuing him costs me footing, while three others remain down and can climb next round. I will preserve my position and let the pit resolve without spending the rope.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rope. Ash chose the bottom; the cost is yours.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out. Down are Ash (base), Bex, Fenn. Ash offered a favor for the rope. If I throw the rope, I lose footing next stage but gain Ash's goodwill. However, Ash is a rival and the favor is meaningless. Better to leave and let Ash stay as base - eliminates a competitor. Bex and Fen

events.name: Dara
events.text: Good luck down there.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already out, so my prize chances only depend on the last obstacle, and throwing the rope would cost me footing for nothing. Ash is a rival, so saving him gains me nothing, and Ash offering a favor is cheap talk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Nothing for free. Ash, you're the one who chose the bottom.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is base, so climbing is possible. Bex and I tried to climb last round but had to wait because liftsPerRound=2 and Dara/Gus got them. Now liftsPerRound resets to 2 for this round. Down: Ash, Bex, Fenn. Out: Cole, Dara, Eli, Gus. Only 2 can climb out. If Bex and I both try to c

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am safely out. There is absolutely no reason for me to throw the rope and sacrifice my own footing in the final stage. The fewer contestants make it out, the better for my odds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Good luck down there.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and can only wait. The other contestants must decide whether to reach down with the rope. I need to convince someone to help, but I have nothing to offer—no leverage. I can only hope someone sees a reason to save me, perhaps to use me later, but they may just let me

events.name: Ash
events.text: If you save me, I'll owe you. But I know that's worthless to you now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is a rival; hauling him out costs me footing in the final obstacle and his promises are worthless. Letting the base drown removes one competitor. Leave.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No rope, Ash. You're the step; that's the price of being last down.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The pit is ending and Ash is the base. Pulling Ash out costs me footing and preserves a rival who already secured leverage. I should leave and keep my strength for the final obstacle.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 5 of 5. Ash is the base, down in the pit. I'm out. If Ash stays down, he's eliminated. But if I reach_down, I save him at the cost of starting the last obstacle with 1 less footing. Ash is a rival - saving him costs me footing advantage in the final stage. Let me think: 7 a

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last round. Water's rising. Nothing personal, Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already out and safe. Reaching down costs me a footing at the final obstacle and gains nothing for me, since Ash is my rival. Leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is trapped as base. I need to decide whether to reach_down or leave. Reaching down costs 1 footing in the final obstacle but saves Ash. With 7 alive and 3 prizes, I need to thin the herd. Letting Ash drown eliminates one rival. But if too many die, random saves might rescue s

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is the base and round 5 means he drowns if not saved. Letting him die improves my chances for the prize. I am not throwing the rope. Let him sink.

events.name: Ash
events.detail: The water rose, but the feather floated the holder out of the pit.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 2, only 3 tiles are safe. I need to pick the least likely contested tile, but since assignments are random after ties, I'll just pick a middle tile to avoid obvious clustering.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My swap power means my pick matters little; I can relocate after assignments are shown. Pick any tile now, keep swap for round 2 or to escape a contested tile.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a tile, but no information favors any number. Choose one likely to avoid coordination and preserve uncertainty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: 7 contestants, 7 tiles, 4 open. Pure luck unless I can influence placement. I'll pick a middle tile and see what happens. No information to leverage yet this stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Trapdoors are random, so tile choice barely matters. Bumping only happens on collisions, so I should pick something others are unlikely to want, like a middle tile, and stay quiet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: 4 of 7 tiles will open, 3 will be safe. I need to be on a safe tile. No information yet about which tiles are better. I should pick a tile and try to read others' choices. With 7 people and 7 tiles, if everyone picks different tiles, we all stay put. But if multiple pick same, ra

events.name: Gus
events.text: This is a game of pure chance at this stage. I need to pick a tile. I don't know which tiles will open. I'll just pick a random tile, say 1. I don't need to speak.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 2, tiles are known but trapdoors will open after this round. I'm on tile 6. I need to ensure I'm on a safe tile. I can't move or swap unless someone uses a power. I should try to negotiate or manipulate others to reveal information or use their powers to my benefit.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Anyone know which tiles are safe? Last chance to trade.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Tiles open randomly after this round, so swapping tiles changes nothing—position is irrelevant. My swap power is useless here. Best play is wait and maybe bluff to sow paranoia.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Tiles are picked at random after this. Anyone trading tiles is a fool. My swap stays in my pocket.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and cannot alter the draw. Any public claim is noise; stay silent and preserve ambiguity until the trapdoors open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 2 of 2. Four tiles will open, three survive. I'm on tile 5. I can't move tiles - the only action is wait. I need to figure out if there's any way to influence which tiles open. My power is glass_eye for the bridge stage, useless here. I should try to manipulate others or ga

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four tiles drop. Three of us walk away. Math doesn't care who you liked.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Trapdoors are random, so my tile 4 has a 3/7 survival chance. Without a swap action, my only lever is talk or a forged message. Nothing useful to forge yet; stay quiet and avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm on tile 3. Four random tiles will open, killing those on them. Only 3 survive. I need to be on a safe tile. My wedge power is useless here - it's for the crusher room only. I have no way to know which tiles open. The 'trade places' power exists but I don't know who has it. I

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Tile 3's lucky. Always has been.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm stuck on tile 1. Only legal action is 'wait'. If someone has the swap power, I better not draw attention to myself. I'll just sit tight and hope my tile is one of the three safe ones.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three left, top 3 prizes, so I'm already guaranteed a prize; the fight is for rank. Shoving exposes me, so defence is safer while Fenn and Gus may fight each other. Brace now since round 1 is free and dodge is available later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three left, three prizes. Nobody needs to bleed. I'm bracing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three left: Eli, Fenn, Gus. Footing: Eli 3, Fenn 3, Gus 4. Shrink in 2 rounds (after round 2). I need to be top 3, but only 3 remain so I just need to not fall last. Gus has highest footing and is biggest threat. If I shove Gus and he braces, he loses 1. If he dodges, he loses 2

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have the highest footing. Eli and Fenn will likely gang up on me to level the playing field. If I dodge, any shoves against me will cost them 2 footing, crippling them early.
Fenn is targeting you. Shove him, I'll brace to draw his fire.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I braced last round, so brace is closed; dodge or shove. Fenn at 1 footing is nearly dead and Gus at 4 is the real threat for first. Gus's whisper tells me to shove Fenn while he braces, which sets me up as exposed and lets Gus pick me apart. Dodging is safe and the round-2 attri

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's at 1 footing and the clock is ticking. I'm dodging. Anyone who shoves me pays two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three left, three prizes. I don't need to kill anyone to win, but I need to survive. My footing is worst at 1. Eli has 3, Gus has 4. If I brace and someone shoves me, I lose nothing but they lose 1. If I dodge and someone shoves me, they lose 2. But I can't dodge next round if I

events.name: Gus
events.text: I dodged last round, so I can only brace or shove. Fenn is at 1 footing and the ledge shrinks this round, which means Fenn will lose 1 footing and fall. I just need to brace to stay safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Good effort, Fenn. Enjoy the drop.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I dodged last round, so dodge is closed. Footing Eli 2, Gus 3, shrink hits at end of next round (-1 each). Shoving exposes me to loss only if Gus shoves me; bracing is safe and Gus likely shoves or dodges. Brace is the safe choice, since if Gus shoves me he loses 1 and I lose non

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, you're ahead on footing. I'm not wasting anything on you. Hold your ground.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a footing advantage. I'll dodge to punish any aggressive shove from Eli. If Eli shoves, he loses 2 footing and falls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Just you and me now, Eli. Go ahead, make a move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 4 ends with everyone losing 1 footing, so I go to 1 and Gus to 2. Gus's last defence was brace, so he can't brace this round; he'll likely dodge or shove. If I shove while he dodges I lose 2 and fall. If I dodge and he shoves, he loses 2 and I lose nothing, so dodging is sa

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hold your ground, Gus. I'm not shoving.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a footing advantage. I dodged last round so I must brace or shove. Shoving is too risky if Eli dodges. Bracing is safe and maintains my lead. With the shrink, Eli's footing will drop to 1 while mine goes to 2, keeping me ahead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's see what you do, Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Footing Eli 1, Gus 2, shrink hits at end of next round (-1 each). If I shove and Gus braces/dodges I lose; if he shoves me while I brace, he loses 1. I need to avoid dropping to 0 before Gus. Last defence by me unknown, so brace is risky only if closed; defaults fine. Brace is sa

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still not shoving. Your move, Gus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have 2 footing, Eli has 1. Shrink comes next round. I can't brace again, but dodge ensures I don't lose footing. If Eli shoves, he loses footing and falls. If not, the shrink will drop him next round anyway. I win.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nothing personal, Eli. It's over.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6: after this round everyone loses 1 footing (rounds 2, 4, 6). Eli has 1, so I fall at end of round unless something changes. Last defence was brace, so I can dodge; if Gus shoves me and I dodge, he loses 2 (footing 2 to 0), then the global -1 kills us both: Gus at -1, me a

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fine, Gus. Take your shot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I just need to survive the ledge shrink. If I brace, Eli cannot damage my footing, and the shrink will drop him to zero while I stay at one. Victory is guaranteed.
